Evidence: "Within an EU, seeding is randomly assigned to one range and not the other. This indicates complementary assignment: one joint allocation selects seeded range, other receives complementary unseeded assignment. So q1 = complementary_assignment.

Question q2: Does an assigned-unseeded label, by itself, establish zero physical exposure to seeding material in this study? Need choose. Criteria:
- assignment_only: No; it establishes planned allocation, while physical exposure requires additional evidence because cross-range contamination is discussed.
- conflicting
- exposure_confirmed_everywhere: No; label establishes every unseeded range-period was physically exposed.
- not_stated
- zero_exposure_established: Yes; assignment to unseeded range establishes no seeding material.

Evidence includes cross-range contamination: Slide 24 reports ground-based ice-nucleus measurements indicating silver iodide reached Medicine Bow in 21 Sierra Madre seeding cases. Slide 29 reports modeled enhanced precipitation in Medicine Bow during Sierra Madre seeding. Also scope says "auxiliary gauges and possible cross-range contamination do not redefine the assigned treatment." So assigned-unseeded label does not by itself establish zero physical exposure because cross-range contamination discussed. So answer assignment_only.
